OVERVIEW Cisco designs and sells a broad range of technologies including hardware, software, and artificial intelligence (AI) powered digital infrastructure to power, help secure, and draw insights from the Internet. We are incorporating AI into our product portfolios across networking, security, collaboration and observability, as well as integrating our products more tightly together into a platform. We are simplifying how our technology is delivered, managed and optimized and helping customers maximize the business value of their technology investments. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: Set forth below and elsewhere in this report and in other documents we file with the SEC are descriptions of the risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from the results contemplated by the forward-looking statements contained in this report. Risks Related to our Business and Industry Our operations can be difficult to predict because our results of operations may fluctuate in future periods. Our results of operations have been in the past, and will continue to be, subject to quarterly and annual fluctuations as a result of numerous factors, some of which may contribute to more pronounced fluctuations in an uncertain global economic environment. Consequently, our results of operations are not a reliable indicator of future results. These factors include: • Customer patterns, such as fluctuating demand for our products and services, especially with respect to service providers and cloud customers; the timing, size, and mix of orders from customers; and changes in sales and implementation cycles for our products and reduced visibility into our customers’ spending plans and associated revenue • Our ability to maintain appropriate inventory levels and purchase commitments and manage manufacturing and customer lead times • Price and product competition in the communications and networking industries, which can change rapidly due to technological innovation and different business models from various geographic regions • Industry trends such as consolidation among our competitors and our customers, and the introduction and market acceptance of new technologies, products and technology standards, and our success in these new and evolving markets and with emerging technologies, including AI • Variations in sales channels, product costs, or mix of products sold (e.g., hardware and software sales, including mix of cloud-based and on-premise software sales) • Fluctuations in our gross margins, and the factors that contribute to such fluctuations • The ability of our direct sale customers, channel partners, contract manufacturers and suppliers to obtain financing, to fund capital expenditures, or withstand financial problems • Actual events, circumstances, outcomes, and amounts differing from judgments, assumptions, and estimates used in determining the values of certain assets (including the amounts of related valuation allowances), liabilities, and other items reflected in our Consolidated Financial Statements • How well we execute on our strategy and operating plans and the impact of changes in our business model that could result in significant restructuring charges • Our ability to achieve targeted cost reductions and anticipated benefits from our investments • Changes in tax laws or accounting rules, or interpretations thereof Any of these factors, or others discussed in this report, could materially harm our business, results of operations, or financial condition. Our results of operations may be negatively impacted by unfavorable economic and market conditions and the uncertain geopolitical environment. Opinions on the Financial Statements and Internal Control over Financial Reporting We have audited the accompanying consolidated balance sheets of Cisco Systems, Inc. and its subsidiaries (the “Company”) as of July 25, 2026 and July 26, 2025, and the related consolidated statements of operations, of comprehensive income, of stockholders' equity and of cash flows for each of the three years in the period ended July 25, 2026, including the related notes (collectively referred to as the “consolidated financial statements”). In our opinion, the consolidated financial statements referred to above present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of the Company as of July 25, 2026 and July 26, 2025, and the results of its operations and its cash flows for each of the three years in the period ended July 25, 2026 in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America. Our responsibility is to express opinions on the Company’s consolidated financial statements and on the Company's internal control over financial reporting based on our audits. credit_strengths.text: Cisco's operating margin sits well above the Information Technology sector median, reflecting a mix shift toward software, security and AI infrastructure that lifted profitability despite modest gross-margin dilution. This pricing power and platform strategy underpin stable internal cash generation, which is the primary source of debt service rather than balance-sheet liquidity.

Operating cash flow comfortably covers capital expenditure, leaving substantial free cash flow after reinvestment. Annual cash generation has been stable across the trend period, and the resulting free-cash-flow-to-debt ratio is consistent with the sector median, indicating that internally generated funds, not asset sales or refinancing, drive repayment capacity.

key_risks.text: Disclosed risk factors highlight fluctuating demand from service providers and cloud customers, order timing and mix volatility, rapid price and product competition, and uncertain global economic and geopolitical conditions. These dynamics make quarterly results an unreliable indicator of future performance and could pressure revenue and margins if customer spending plans weaken or inventory commitments prove misaligned.

The debt structure carries meaningful near-term maturities, with a large current debt balance falling due within the next twelve months alongside additional maturities in subsequent years. Refinancing this profile at higher rates would raise interest expense, and the current ratio below one indicates that current liabilities, including maturing debt, modestly exceed current assets.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage is strong and broadly in line with the sector median, while gross and net leverage remain modest relative to peers. The indicative financial risk profile is minimal, with substantial headroom before the next leverage threshold, suggesting that a moderate EBITDA decline or incremental debt would not immediately impair the credit profile.

Free cash flow covers a substantial portion of total debt, and cash on hand provides a liquidity buffer, though the current ratio below one means working-capital liabilities absorb much of that liquidity. Shareholder distributions and buybacks consume most free cash flow, leaving less cushion for debt reduction or unexpected funding needs.

overall_credit_view.text: Cisco presents a minimal indicative financial risk profile, supported by scale, high operating margins and consistent cash generation. Leverage is below the sector median and coverage is adequate, while the debt maturity profile is manageable given annual free cash flow. The credit view is stable, with refinancing and shareholder returns the key variables to monitor.

Analyst judgement: the principal sensitivity is a sustained demand downturn in service provider and cloud spending, which could compress margins and cash flow just as near-term maturities require refinancing. Conversely, continued AI-driven product momentum and disciplined cost control would preserve headroom. The Altman Z double-prime grey zone and below-one current ratio warrant monitoring but do not alter the overall assessment.

credit_strengths.text: Cisco的營業利潤率遠高於資訊科技行業中位數，反映業務組合轉向軟件、保安及人工智能基礎設施，儘管毛利率略有攤薄，仍提升盈利能力。此定價能力及平台策略支撐穩定的內部現金產生，而內部現金產生是償還債務的主要來源，而非資產負債表流動性。
營運現金流足以覆蓋資本開支，再投資後仍留下大量自由現金流。年度現金產生在趨勢期內保持穩定，由此產生的自由現金流對債務比率與行業中位數一致，表明償債能力由內部產生的資金驅動，而非資產出售或再融資。

key_risks.text: 披露的風險因素凸顯服務供應商及雲端客戶需求波動、訂單時間及組合波動、價格及產品競爭激烈，以及全球經濟及地緣政治狀況不明朗。這些動態使季度業績成為未來表現的不可靠指標，若客戶支出計劃減弱或庫存承諾出現錯配，可能對收入及利潤率構成壓力。
債務結構包含有意義的近期到期債務，大量流動債務餘額將於未來十二個月內到期，隨後數年亦有額外到期債務。以較高利率為此債務結構再融資將增加利息支出，而流動比率低於一表明流動負債（包括到期債務）略高於流動資產。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率強勁，與行業中位數大致一致，而總槓桿及淨槓桿相對同業仍屬溫和。指示性財務風險狀況為極低，距離下一個槓桿門檻有充足緩衝，表明EBITDA適度下降或債務增加不會立即損害信用狀況。
自由現金流覆蓋總債務的相當部分，手頭現金提供流動性緩衝，儘管流動比率低於一意味著營運資金負債吸收大部分流動性。股東分派及回購消耗大部分自由現金流，用於削減債務或應對意外資金需求的緩衝較少。

overall_credit_view.text: Cisco呈現極低的指示性財務風險狀況，受規模、高營業利潤率及穩定現金產生支撐。槓桿低於行業中位數，覆蓋率充足，而鑑於年度自由現金流，債務到期結構屬可控。信用觀點穩定，再融資及股東回報是需監測的關鍵變數。
分析師判斷：主要敏感因素為服務供應商及雲端支出的持續需求下滑，可能在近期到期債務需要再融資之際壓縮利潤率及現金流。相反，持續的人工智能驅動產品勢頭及嚴謹的成本控制將保持緩衝。Altman Z double-prime灰色區域及低於一的流動比率值得監測，但不改變整體評估。
